landscape.summary: The chain from a Gemini image to a UE 5.8 landscape is verified at both ends and broken in one place in the middle. Ends: Epic's 5.8 docs fix the contract (16-bit single-channel heightmap, 8-bit single-channel weightmaps at the landscape's resolution, N+1 sizes, -256..255.992 m at Z scale 100), and the ground truth already proves the heightmap push (R1) and creation (R-CREATE). Gemini cannot supply 16-bit data: the API docs expose only image/png and image/jpeg with no bit-depth control, the API pricing page (2026-10-09) lists every image model as "Not available" on the free tier, so the free route is the Gemini app (Nano Banana 2, 1K download without a plan). A local run on this machine shows the standard 8-to-16-bit expansion (float smoothing, x257, uint16 PNG) takes a JPEG-degraded 202-level image to 51,169 distinct levels; the project's own erosion/stamp scripts add fractal detail afterwards. Layer classification is available (cv2 5.0 k-means in Lab runs here), and the weightmap import API exists in the stub and engine source (reads the R channel, quantises to 8-bit, needs Layer Info Objects assigned and an RT at least the landscape size). The break: no Python surface creates a LandscapeLayerInfoObject or adds a target layer (no factory in the stub, target_layers read-only, AddTargetLayer not a UFUNCTION, and the project's C++ plugin imports zero layers), and the weightmap import has never been run on this machine. The proven alternative here composites baked RGB weight textures in the material, not landscape paint layers. Corrections: Gaea 2 Community is non-commercial and exports at most 1024x1024 (not UE-legal); World Machine Basic is non-commercial at 1025x1025; the material builder is scripts/make_landscape_material.py and does not use LandscapeLayerBlend; TerraFusion is PolyForm Noncommercial; Infinigen has no native Windows terrain; only Depth Anything Small/DA3 Small/Base/Mono/Metric and MoGe are permissively licensed. No verified method rectifies an oblique depth map into a top-down heightmap. Terrain Diffusion (MIT, SIGGRAPH 2026, last commit 2026-08-12, GeoTIFF elevation output, hand-drawn coarse-map conditioning) is the only open sketch-to-heightmap model found with weights and a shippable licence, untested on sm_120.

The PNG importer (LandscapeFileFormatPng.cpp) accepts 8-bit PNGs with a warning and expands G8 to G16 via FImageCore::CopyImage, which computes (Src << 8) | Src = value x 257, so one 8-bit grey step = 257 counts = 200.78 cm, i.e. 2.0 m to the stated precision (exactly 2.0 m only if the operator pre-converts with value x 256). Height is multiplied by Z scale, so the (Z/100) x 2 m generalisation holds. Minor precision note only: the UE-native 8-bit riser is 2.008 m, not exactly 2.000 m, and the terrace height applies when the 8-bit source uses its full 0-255 range imported directly; any rescale into a narrower 16-bit band shrinks the riser proportionally with total relief. recommendations: Verified chain (free tier): Gemini app (Nano Banana 2, 1K download) produces (a) a top-down greyscale relief image and (b) a top-down painted biome map -> host Python: decode JPEG to float grey, bilateral + Gaussian smooth, x257 to uint16, crop/resample to 1009 or 2017 (resample_heightmap.py), optionally add relief via composite_stamps.py and terrain_erosion.hydraulic_droplets, write 16-bit PNG -> push with R1 (existing landscape) or R-CREATE (new) -> cv2.kmeans in Lab on the biome map (K = layer count), map clusters to layer names by centroid colour, write one 8-bit PNG mask per layer at landscape size -> weightmap push via landscape_import_weightmap_from_render_target -> material built with MaterialEditingLibrary using MaterialExpressionLandscapeLayerBlend. Only the last two arrows are unexecuted.

Weakest link: Layer Info Objects. Either accept one manual step (Landscape Mode > Paint > create Layer Info per layer, once per project) or extend LandscapeLab/Plugins/LandscapeLabEditor with a UFUNCTION that creates ULandscapeLayerInfoObject assets and calls ALandscapeProxy::AddTargetLayer / passes FLandscapeImportLayerInfo at Import; then run landscape_import_weightmap_from_render_target once and record it as a recipe before trusting it.

Proven fallback that avoids layer infos entirely: bake the k-means class masks into an RGB(A) weight texture and composite in the material exactly as make_layer_weightmap.py + make_landscape_material.py already do (max 3-4 layers per texture); this is the only layer route proven on this machine.

Treat Gemini greyscale relief as a low-frequency guide only: measure unique levels and JPEG blocking on real downloads before adopting; if the 1K map fails, use Terrain Diffusion (MIT) with the Gemini map as the hand-drawn coarse conditioning, converting its GeoTIFF elevation to uint16 with rasterio/gdal_translate -ot UInt16 -scale.

Do not use Gaea 2 Community or World Machine Basic output in the shipped game (both non-commercial, and 1024/1025 are not UE-legal sizes); do not use TerraFusion (PolyForm Noncommercial), Depth Anything V2 Base/Large/Giant or DA3 Large/Giant (CC BY-NC), or Marigold weights (RAIL++-M) without a licence review.
For oblique concept art use DA3-SMALL/BASE/METRIC-LARGE or MoGe-2 (Apache/MIT) only as relative-relief hints; no rectification to top-down is verified, so do not promise a heightmap from oblique art.
For real places, download Copernicus GLO-30, keep the attribution string, resample to 1009/2017 and scale to UInt16 (datum 32768) with rasterio.

Water: enable Water + Landmass (Experimental/Beta) in the project, spawn WaterBodyRiver with EditorActorSubsystem.spawn_actor_from_class, set points on spline_comp (set_spline_points, world space) from the classified river centreline, call k2_synchronize_and_broadcast_data_change, then verify carving by render; file the result as a recipe before relying on it.

refuted: 'The Gaea Community Edition is licensed for commercial use' (CG Channel, Gaea 1.3.2 era, 2022): for Gaea 2.x the vendor page says 'The Community Edition is free for non-commercial use' (quadspinner.com/gaea; cgchannel.com 2025-07-15).
'Gaea Community exports 1K that UE can import directly': the cap is 1024x1024 (quadspinner.com/download, 2.3.1.0, 9/24/2026), and 1024 is not an N+1 size; crop to 1009.
'World Machine free edition gives a UE-ready 1K heightmap': the cap is 1025x1025 and non-commercial (world-machine.com/download.php, purchase.php); crop to 1009.

'The Gemini API free tier can generate images': the pricing page (2026-10-09) lists every image model as 'Not available' on the Free tier; only the Gemini app generates for free (Nano Banana 2, 1K download).
'Gemini can output a 16-bit PNG heightmap': the API docs expose only image/png and image/jpeg with no bit-depth control; no 16-bit option is documented.

'make_landscape_material lives in scripts/c0_build_materials.py and builds LandscapeLayerBlend nodes' (as the brief stated): the builder is scripts/make_landscape_material.py and grep finds no LandscapeLayerBlend in any script; import_heightmap.py:2473 records it is 'a weightmap LinearInterpolate composite, not a LandscapeLayerBlend'.

'Python can create landscape layer infos / target layers in 5.8': no LandscapeLayerInfoObjectFactory in the stub, Landscape.target_layers is Read-Only, ALandscapeProxy::AddTargetLayer has no UFUNCTION (LandscapeProxy.h:1606-1609).

'The weightmap render target must be exactly the landscape size / needs 16-bit data': LandscapeEdit.cpp:8432 only requires at least the landscape size on each axis, and :8400-8402 quantises the R channel to 8-bit.
'Marigold is Apache-2.0': only the code is; the weights are CreativeML Open RAIL++-M (github.com/prs-eth/Marigold; HF model card).
'Depth Anything V2 is Apache-2.0': only Small is; Base/Large/Giant are CC-BY-NC-4.0. DA3 likewise: Small/Base/Metric-Large/Mono-Large Apache-2.0, Large/Giant CC BY-NC 4.0.
'TerraFusion is open for commercial use': PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 (github.com/millennium-nova/terra-fusion).
'Infinigen generates terrain natively on Windows': its platform table marks native Windows terrain unsupported and WSL2 terrain Experimental (docs/source/Installation.md).
'A.N.T. Landscape ships inside Blender': it is an extension (v0.2.0, May 2024, 4.2+) and is absent from the local Blender 5.2 addons_core folder.
'Infinigen exports heightmaps for Unreal': its exporter writes OBJ/FBX/STL/PLY/USD meshes only and never mentions Unreal or heightmaps.

scenes.summary: The verified chain from a Gemini concept painting to a lit UE 5.8 scene now has primary-source backing for every link except two: (a) the back-projection step (pinhole equations and UE axis constants are verified; the composed pixel-plus-depth to UE-centimetre transform has not been run on this machine) and (b) the camera solver on painted, non-photographic input (GeoCalib, DA3 and MoGe-2 are documented on photos only). Detection: the Gemini API docs (updated 2026-09-23) give box_2d as [ymin,xmin,ymax,xmax] normalised 0-1000, and segmentation masks as polygons of [x,y] normalised 0-1000, which refutes the widely repeated 'base64 PNG probability mask' claim. The free tier is explicitly 'Used to improve our products: Yes' with human review. Local open-vocabulary options are SAM 3 (custom SAM License, gated weights, Python 3.12+), Grounding DINO (Apache-2.0, stale since 2024) and Florence-2 (MIT). Depth and camera: Depth Anything 3 (Small/Base/Metric-Large/Mono-Large Apache-2.0; Large/Giant/Nested CC BY-NC) outputs intrinsics and metric depth via focal*out/300; MoGe-2 ViT-L is MIT with metric scale and FOV estimation; GeoCalib (Apache-2.0 code, CC BY 4.0 weights, CPU-capable) gives focal, roll and pitch from one image. UniDepth and PerspectiveFields are non-commercial; fSpy is a dormant GUI (last release 2019). World models: none of HunyuanWorld-Voyager (60 GB), Gen3C (~43 GB), DreamScene (>40 GB) fit 16 GB; WorldGen (Apache-2.0, ~10 GB low-VRAM, needs gated FLUX.1-dev) and Matrix-3D (MIT, 12 GB) do on paper, Linux-only; Marble's free plan cannot export. Splats reach UE 5.8 through the XGRIDS LCC plugin (v3.3.1, 2026-08-17, proprietary free tier); NanoGS is MIT but 5.6/5.7 only. UE side: spawn, transform, ground trace with HitResult.to_dict(), the full lighting stack, manual exposure, CineCamera focal/filmback (HFOV = 2*atan(sensorWidth/(2*focal)) in engine source) and SceneCapture2D PNG export (RTF_RGBA8 required) are all confirmed in the 5.8.1 stub or proven in the local recipes. The camera solve ('Phase B') remains the one unbuilt stage.

recommendations: Build the scene stage as this chain, each link above is verified unless marked: Gemini free API (2D box_2d + label JSON, thinking 'minimal') -> GeoCalib on CPU for focal/roll/pitch -> DA3METRIC-LARGE (Apache-2.0) or MoGe-2 ViT-L (MIT) in the WSL trellis env for metric depth and intrinsics -> back-project each box's bottom-centre pixel with the pinhole equations into UE (Forward=X, Right=Y, Up=Z, cm) [inferred, test first] -> placements.json -> EditorActorSubsystem.spawn_actor_from_class + set_actor_transform -> line_trace_single top-down with HitResult.to_dict() for ground Z -> apply_lighting.py recipe -> CineCameraActor with current_focal_length = sensor_width/(2*tan(HFOV/2)) or CameraComponent.field_of_view -> SceneCapture2D RTF_RGBA8 PNG -> LPIPS/DreamSim/DINOv2 score plus Gemini critique.

Before trusting any solver on paintings, run a calibration test: render a known UE scene (known HFOV, camera height, pitch, marker actors at known positions), feed the PNG to GeoCalib and DA3/MoGe-2, back-project the markers and measure the position error; adopt the pipeline only if the error is below the kit's placement tolerance.

Exclude on licence or fit: PerspectiveFields (Adobe Research noncommercial), UniDepth (CC BY-NC), DA3-Large/Giant/Nested (CC BY-NC), SceneScript, HunyuanWorld-Voyager (60 GB), Gen3C (~43 GB), DreamScene (>40 GB), Holodeck and LayoutVLM (paid OpenAI API, non-UE outputs), Marble Free plan (no export).

If an 'image to world' backdrop is wanted, trial WorldGen (Apache-2.0, ~10 GB low-VRAM, PLY splat + mesh; note FLUX.1-dev gating and 25 GB disk) or Matrix-3D (MIT, 12 GB for the 5B low-VRAM path) in WSL2, and bring the PLY splat into UE 5.8 with the XGRIDS LCC plugin free tier; treat the result as reference/backdrop, never as modular geometry.

For the UE side, reuse the proven scripts: never positional unreal.Rotator, save the touched actors' own packages, set render_target_format = RTF_RGBA8 before export_render_target, set always_persist_rendering_state on the capture component, and ignore WorldPartitionHLOD proxies when tracing for ground.

For the Gemini judge, keep it advisory: free-tier inputs and outputs are used for product improvement with human review, so send only the operator's own renders and Gemini images, and measure every number it proposes before adoption (the existing gemini_critique_prompt.md practice).

Enable HDRIBackdrop and SunPosition in the project only if needed; Sun Position gives a real-world sun elevation/azimuth from latitude, date and time, which can seed apply_lighting.py's elevation_deg/azimuth_deg when a concept implies a place and hour.

'Gemini free-tier data is not used for training': the pricing page marks every free-tier model 'Used to improve our products: Yes' and the terms say human reviewers may read and annotate API input and output.
'PerspectiveFields is open for commercial use': its LICENSE is the Adobe Research License, noncommercial only.
'fSpy is maintained and scriptable': latest release v1.0.3 on 2019-01-02, last push 2022-12-08, Electron GUI; the repo moved from stuffmatic/fSpy to perarnia/fSpy.
'UniDepth can ship in a commercial game': CC BY-NC 4.0.
'Depth Anything 3 is entirely Apache-2.0': DA3-LARGE-1.1, DA3-GIANT-1.1 and DA3NESTED-GIANT-LARGE-1.1 are CC BY-NC 4.0; only Small, Base, Metric-Large and Mono-Large are Apache 2.0.
'HunyuanWorld-1.0-lite runs on 16 GB': the README only claims consumer GPUs 'such as 4090' (24 GB); no 16 GB figure exists.
'World Labs Marble free tier exports splats': the Free plan can generate but not export; commercial rights need Pro.
'NanoGS supports UE 5.8': the README lists UE 5.6 and 5.7 only; the LCC plugin is the one listing 5.8.
'SAM 2 installs natively on Windows': the repo strongly recommends WSL with Ubuntu and compiles a CUDA kernel.
'create_render_target2d + export_render_target writes a PNG': the default format is RTF_RGBA16F and the export writes OpenEXR under the .png name; RTF_RGBA8 is required (local RECIPES.md 12030).
'AEM_MANUAL fixes a white SceneCapture': the fix is always_persist_rendering_state (local RECIPES.md 12146).
'HitResult fields are readable as Python properties in 5.8': the stub exposes none and break_hit_result does not exist; use to_dict() (local LESSONS.md 10814).
'Epic MCP CaptureViewport returns an MCP image': it returns base64 inside a text result (TownFrom2D findings, engine source cited there).
'SceneTools.trace_world returns a ground Z': it returns the distance from start to hit (TownFrom2D findings).

gemini-free.summary: As of 2026-10-10 Google's own pages split "free Gemini" into two very different things. (1) The Gemini app (gemini.google.com, no subscription) generates and edits images for free with Nano Banana 2; Nano Banana 2.1 and "redo with Nano Banana Pro" require a Google AI plan; free downloads are 1K (the local manifests show 1024x1024, 1408x768, 1433x736 JPGs); every image carries an invisible SynthID watermark and Content Credentials, while the visible sparkle can be switched off in Settings > Media Watermark; Google publishes no numeric daily cap (limits are "compute-based", refresh every 5 hours, "may change without notice"); free-plan chats are used for training and human review unless Keep Activity is off. (2) The Gemini API / AI Studio free tier (no billing) has NO image generation at all: the pricing page dated 2026-10-09 shows "Not available" in the Free Tier column for gemini-nano-banana-2.1, gemini-3.1-flash-image, gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image, gemini-3-pro-image and gemini-2.5-flash-image, and Google's Feb-26-2026 launch post says a paid API key is required even inside AI Studio. What IS free on the API is vision: gemini-3.8-flash, gemini-2.5-flash, gemini-2.5-pro, gemini-3-flash-preview and gemini-robotics-er-2-preview are "Free of charge", with structured JSON, [ymin,xmin,ymax,xmax] 0-1000 boxes, polygon masks, [y,x] points, 20 MB inline requests, 3,600 images per request and a free Files API (20 GB, 48 h). Per-model free RPM/RPD numbers are no longer on the public rate-limits page; they are only shown in the AI Studio dashboard. Free API use is explicitly "used to improve our products" with human review, outputs are not claimed by Google, and the only training restriction is "models that compete". The SDK is google-genai 2.29.0 (PyPI upload 2026-10-07, Python >=3.10, Apache-2.0), with both the new Interactions API and the legacy generate_content. Gemini CLI 0.63.0 still exists (Apache-2.0) but its free "Login with Google" path was replaced by Antigravity CLI on 2026-06-18; the unpaid API-key path is 250 requests/day Flash-only and the nanobanana extension needs a paid key. Corrected: free API image generation, 500-1000 free AI Studio images/day, Imagen in the app, base64 PNG masks, and the 1,000/day Gemini CLI quota are all false or stale today. Pipeline consequence: images are produced manually in the app; the API is used free only for analysis.

verifier_votes.reason: The plugin log line and the Gemini unpaid-services quote are confirmed verbatim (ModelContextProtocolServer.cpp line 446, UE_LOGF Warning; ai.google.dev terms effective 2026-03-23). But the claim is imprecise in three ways. (1) Section 6(e) was readable: WebFetch got 403, but curl with a browser User-Agent returned HTTP 200 (297 KB) for https://www.unrealengine.com/en-US/eula/unreal, so 'until Section 6(e) is read' is no longer a valid hedge. The actual 6(e) text restricts 'using the Licensed Technology as a training input to any Generative AI Program or as prompt-based input where the Generative AI Program trains on input data', plus a separate bar on using 'MetaHuman digital characters and animation curves (or any rendered output thereof ...)' to build/enhance any database or train/test any AI. recommendations: Repo layout for Gemini2UE: CLAUDE.md as a <=200-line index (docs: target under 200 lines, 4 MiB skip, imports max 4 hops), topic rules in .claude/rules/*.md, stage skills in .claude/skills/<stage>/SKILL.md (<500 lines, disable-model-invocation: true for side-effect stages), judge/auditor subagents in .claude/agents/, hooks ported from UE5LandscapePipeline/.claude/hooks/guard.py (exit 2 = block, 20 s timeouts), and .mcp.json {"unreal-mcp":{"type":"http","url":"http://127.0.0.1:8001/mcp","timeout":600000}} with MCP_TIMEOUT raised for slow editor starts.

Batch steps: run `claude -p` with `--output-format json --json-schema <schema>` and `--allowedTools "Read,Bash(python *)"`; add `--permission-prompts none` for unattended runs and `--bare --mcp-config .mcp.json` when the step must not inherit hooks; parse `.structured_output` with jq; never run `-p` without --bare in an untrusted folder because it auto-runs that folder's hooks and MCP servers.

Gemini as judge must stay on the FREE tier: use a free vision model (gemini-2.5-flash or gemini-3.8-flash; image models are 'Not available' free) with response_mime_type='application/json' + response_schema and seed/temperature pinned; keep images <=20 MB inline and ~6 tiles each; read the actual RPM/RPD from the AI Studio rate-limit page after creating a key, since the docs publish none; record model id, date, prompt hash and the JSON verdict next to the render; treat scores as advice and measure before adopting (proven pattern).

Before any image goes to Gemini (API or app): run scripts/ai_input_guard.py --strict; exclude renders containing Fab 'Allows usage with AI: No' assets and, until UE EULA 6(e) is read, renders dominated by Epic Licensed Technology (MetaHuman, Epic sample content), because Unpaid Services use submitted content to improve products. If the app route is used, turn Keep Activity off for critique sessions.

Local metric gate first, Gemini second: SSIM via cv2.quality.QualitySSIM_compute on the host (87 ms at 1080p, no install) and LPIPS alex in the WSL trellis env (33 ms at 512^2, 237 ms at 1080p on CPU, installed with pip --target to leave the proven env untouched); add DINOv2 ViT-L/14 cosine similarity using the 1.2 GB weights already cached in WSL; defer DreamSim (MIT, Linux, unmeasured) until a GPU slot is free.

Licensing register: keep ASSETS.md + CREDITS.md + recipes/ai_restrictions.json unchanged; extend MANIFEST.json per Gemini image with sha256, size_px, model/app name, generation date, prompt text, SynthID=true, operator name, and 'operator-owned AI output' per Google ToS; mark every TRELLIS/Hunyuan output row with model, licence, reference hashes and seed; store the FBX/sha256 as the artefact of record because TRELLIS is not bit-reproducible and Gemini image generation exposes no seed.

Git LFS for the new repo: `* text=auto` first, then `*.uasset *.umap *.fbx *.glb *.png *.jpg *.exr filter=lfs diff=lfs merge=lfs -text`; GitHub Free gives 10 GiB storage and 10 GiB bandwidth per month with a 2 GB per-file cap, so keep _verify renders and model weights out of LFS and budget uasset churn.

Disk plan under 24.8 GB free: reclaimable now are LandscapeLab/DerivedDataCache/VT (14 GB, rebuildable), Saved/Screenshots 1.6 GB, Logs 466 MB, Profiling 393 MB, Crashes 324 MB, Zen local store 5.4 GB (rebuildable), host pip cache 165 MB (`pip cache purge`); for the new project set UE-LocalDataCachePath to a dedicated folder and rely on UnusedFileAge=34 pruning; run `wsl --manage Ubuntu-24.04 --set-sparse true` after `wsl --shutdown` and prune /opt/miniforge3 (11 GB) before adding any model: Hunyuan3D-2 needs ~4.93 GB (shape) + 9.19 GB (paint), SAM3 3.44 GB (gated), Depth Anything V2 Small only 99.2 MB and Apache-2.0.

Safety: keep the UE MCP server and Python remote execution on 127.0.0.1 (MCP has no auth; remote exec runs arbitrary Python), never set RemoteExecutionMulticastBindAddress to 0.0.0.0 or TTL to 1, never set an HTTPServer DefaultBindAddress, do not expose 8001/6766/6776 through the Windows firewall or port-forward them to WSL, and run the MCP server only while a pipeline step needs it (bAutoStartServer=false).

'Gemini image generation takes a seed for reproducible images' — google-genai 2.29.0 ImageConfig has no seed field; GenerateContentConfig.seed is 'best effort'; Imagen's seed is unavailable when add_watermark is true; the image-generation docs name no seed and state all images carry SynthID.
'MCP_TIMEOUT controls MCP tool-call timeouts' — MCP_TIMEOUT is the server startup timeout (30 s default); tool-call timeouts are MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT or the per-server `timeout` field in .mcp.json.

'UE Python remote execution is exposed on the LAN by default' — defaults are bind 127.0.0.1 and multicast TTL 0 (local host only); exposure requires changing them.

textures-materials.summary: The fully verified chain is: Gemini FREE tier in the Gemini app (not the API: every Gemini API image model shows "Free tier: Not available" on the pricing page dated 2026-10-09, so the only free source is the consumer app, where images download at 1K without an AI plan and arrive as JPEG; measured here at 1408x768 RGB JPEG) -> seamless edges with img2texture (MIT, pip, ran on host Python 3.12: 1408x768 -> 1127x615 at --overlap 0.2, so about 20 percent of the image is spent on the blend) or an offset-and-blend in OpenCV -> optional 4x upscale with Real-ESRGAN (BSD-3-Clause code and repo-hosted weights; portable realesrgan-ncnn-vulkan-20220424-windows.zip on release v0.2.5.0) -> normal and height from the albedo with DeepBump (GPL-3.0, ships cli.py, ran outside Blender on host Python 3.12 with onnxruntime 1.31.0 CPU in 2.56 s for colour-to-normals and 0.80 s for normals-to-height on a 1408x768 image), with a numpy/OpenCV Sobel normal (0.12 s) and the repo's own derive_material_maps.py as the always-works baseline -> 8-bit PNGs imported through AssetImportTask with the proven settings (albedo sRGB True TC_DEFAULT; normal sRGB False TC_NORMALMAP; roughness sRGB False TC_MASKS; all TA_WRAP), set after import and read back -> master material and MaterialInstanceConstant through MaterialEditingLibrary using the legacy MP_BASE_COLOR / MP_ROUGHNESS / MP_NORMAL pins, which work under Substrate because non-Substrate graphs are converted at compile time (documented, and proven on this machine where LandscapeLab has had r.Substrate=True since 2026-07-28). Substrate itself defaults off at the CVar (r.Substrate=0 in RenderUtils.cpp) and is written as True into DefaultEngine.ini only for newly created projects by GameProjectUtils.cpp; Epic still labels it Beta. The 16-bit single-channel PNG trap (TC_Alpha renders nothing, TC_Masks gives a shine defect) stays real; DeepBump and Sobel outputs are 8-bit, ambientCG normals and displacement are 16-bit. Corrections: no Gemini API free tier for images; Materialize has no CLI and no GitHub release; MaterialGAN needs calibrated multi-flash captures and is deprecated; Material Anything takes a mesh, not a texture; Upscayl's UltraSharp weights are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; the Intrinsic decomposition repo is academic-use only. Weakest links: the manual, un-guaranteed-tileable Gemini app input, and roughness, which no free single-image tool measures (it is authored).

recommendations: Treat the Gemini FREE tier as the Gemini app only: every Gemini API image model is 'Free tier: Not available' (pricing page 2026-10-09), so the input stage is a named manual step (operator prompts in the app, downloads 1K JPEG, drops into Free/gemini_vN with a MANIFEST row). Seamless step: run img2texture (MIT) with --overlap 0.2 and accept the shrink (1408x768 -> 1127x615), or implement the equivalent offset-and-blend in OpenCV to keep full size; measure tileability with an edge-difference metric on a 2x2 tile before import, since Google publishes no tileable-texture guidance.

PBR derivation: DeepBump CLI (GPL-3, run as a separate process with PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8) for normal and height; keep scripts/derive_material_maps.py (Sobel, measured DX convention) as the fallback and for roughness, and record roughness as AUTHORED, not derived; run classify_convention on every normal before import.

Upscale only when needed with realesrgan-ncnn-vulkan (BSD-3, release v0.2.5.0 assets) using the bundled realesrgan-x4plus weights; do not ship outputs of CC BY-NC-SA community models (UltraSharp) and verify Remacri's licence before use.

Import with the proven AssetImportTask pattern from scripts/import_surface_set.py and the R-DERIVEMAT value table (albedo sRGB True TC_DEFAULT; normal sRGB False TC_NORMALMAP; roughness sRGB False TC_MASKS; TA_WRAP), always set properties after import and read them back; route any 16-bit single-channel source through scripts/texture_16bit.py.

Only move to MaterialExpressionSubstrateSlabBSDF + MP_FRONT_MATERIAL if a Substrate-only feature is needed, and remember Substrate is still Beta per Epic.
Capture recompile_material's returned list and the log, and verify by render (not read-back), per LOCAL_GROUND_TRUTH refuted claims.
Use ambientCG (CC0, keyless v2 JSON API) as the calibration and fallback library; remember its NormalDX/NormalGL and Displacement maps are 16-bit.

refuted: 'Gemini API / AI Studio image generation has a free tier': the pricing page (2026-10-09) marks Free tier 'Not available' for Gemini 3 Pro Image, 3.1 Flash Image, 3.1 Flash Lite Image, 2.5 Flash Image and Nano Banana 2.1; only the consumer Gemini app is free.

'Substrate is on by default in UE 5.8 for every project': the r.Substrate CVar defaults to 0 in RenderUtils.cpp; only newly created projects get r.Substrate=True written by GameProjectUtils.cpp, existing projects stay non-Substrate, and Epic still labels it Beta.

'Python material building needs Substrate nodes once Substrate is enabled': legacy MaterialProperty pins compile under Substrate (compile-time conversion documented by Epic; proven in LandscapeLab with r.Substrate=True since 2026-07-28).
'DeepBump is a Blender-only add-on': it ships cli.py and ran on host Python 3.12 without Blender; the doc's onnxruntime==1.15.1 pin is not required (1.31.0 worked).
'MaterialGAN estimates PBR from one photo': it needs calibrated camera/light positions and multiple flash photos and was deprecated 2023-04-07.
'Material Anything turns a texture image into PBR maps': its input is a 3D mesh (.glb); it renders multi-view material maps for an object.
'All ambientCG PNG maps are 8-bit': the 2026-08-03 sweep in RECIPES.md found 15 of 35 maps 16-bit (NormalDX/NormalGL RGB, Displacement grey).
'Real-ESRGAN's latest GitHub release carries the Windows binary': v0.3.0 (2022-09-20) has no assets; the windows zip and .pth weights are on v0.2.5.0 (2022-04-24).
'Upscayl's bundled models are all commercially usable': UltraSharp's Hugging Face card is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
'img2texture keeps the source resolution': it shrinks the image (1408x768 -> 1127x615 at --overlap 0.2) because the seam blend consumes the overlap.
'The compphoto Intrinsic decomposition model is open for any use': the README says 'provided for academic use only'.

PCGPythonInterop has no README; its contents are two PCG nodes (Execute Python Script, Python Data Processor) and the UPCGPythonDataBridge helper, documented only in the headers.

The project DerivedDataCache folder in LandscapeLab is not the Zen or Local DDC; the whole 14 GB is the [VirtualTextureChunkDDCCache] store at %GAMEDIR%DerivedDataCache/VT, while the Zen local store lives at AppData/Local/UnrealEngine/Common/Zen (5.4 GB).

image-to-3d-props.summary: What holds: the local TRELLIS stage (R-FORGE stage 3) stays untextured because its texture bake (`postprocessing_utils.to_glb`) needs the Gaussian output rendered through mip-splatting's `diff_gaussian_rasterization` plus `nvdiffrast`; both carry non-commercial licences (NVIDIA 1-Way Commercial; Inria/MPI Gaussian-Splatting), so the bake cannot be added for a shipped game even though sm_120 builds of those extensions are documented (TRELLIS issue #243, torch 2.7.1+cu128). `diffoctreerast` is not needed for the bake. TRELLIS.2 (MIT, PBR GLB) officially needs 24 GB, is Linux-only, pulls nvdiffrast v0.4.0 and nvdiffrec (both non-commercial) in setup.sh, and has open, unresolved Blackwell failures on 16 GB cards (TRELLIS.2 #102 RTX 5080; FlexGEMM #32 RTX 5070 Laptop on exactly this machine's torch 2.11.0+cu128/WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 stack); only 32 GB RTX 5090 setups are reported working. Pixal3D (TencentARC, MIT, May 2026, SIGGRAPH 2026) is the best-fitting open PBR model on paper (low-VRAM mode, ~11 GB peak at 1024, multi-view inference since Sept 2026, Windows 16 GB Ada run in the ComfyUI wrapper) but it is built on TRELLIS.2 and inherits the same FlexGEMM sm_120 risk and licence chain. The one route with open code, licence text, VRAM figures and Blackwell evidence all opened is Hunyuan3D-2 (2.0 shape + Paint): official 16 GB total, Windows supported, Paint can texture an existing mesh, and the YanWenKun Windows portable v4-cu129 (torch 2.8.0, CUDA 12.9, "Full support for Blackwell (50 series) GPUs", ≥6 GB VRAM for texture with offload) runs it natively; its blocker is the Tencent licence, which excludes the EU, UK and South Korea for use and display of Output and caps at 1M MAU. MV-Adapter (Apache-2.0, <10 GB SD2.1 image+geometry texturing of an existing mesh) is the only licence-clean texture-stage candidate found, with no Blackwell evidence yet. Hosted: Meshy free tier is 100 credits/month under CC BY 4.0 (commercial with credit) but has no API; Rodin, Sloyd and Anything World free tiers are non-commercial/personal or revenue-capped; Tripo pages returned 403, so its free-tier licence stays unverified; Hunyuan3D 2.5/3.0/3.1 have no public repos. Corrected: TRELLIS.2 "low VRAM 8 GB" claims exist only on third-party blogs; the default TRELLIS.2 export writes WebP textures, which UE 5.8.1's glTF parser cannot read (PNG/JPEG only).

town-and-kits.summary: The only proven route on this machine from a town plan to placed buildings is R-TOWNKIT: plan_city.py (organic layout, heightmap + required water-mask npz) -> town_kit_manifest.py -> C++ SpawnKitHouse/SetKitInstances (ISM per Nanite module) -> census verify -> foliage clear -> save -> navmesh -> HLOD, measured at 349 houses / 18,329 instances / 371 streets with cobbled streets as a landscape-material mask. Its contract is a plain JSON plan whose building rows carry loc_cm, size_cm (on a 50 cm snap), storeys, yaw_deg, door_side and roof_candidate, and whose street rows are <=15 m segments with width_cm. Nothing in that chain reads an image: the adapter the Gemini pipeline needs is a third plan.layout that emits those rows from CV output. The CV stack is installable today on host Python 3.12 (shapely 2.2.0, vtracer 0.6.15, sknw 0.15 + numba 0.68.0, networkx, scikit-image; cv2.ximgproc.thinning present), and the segmentation->skeleton->vectorise pipeline is published for scanned historical maps with >94 % completeness, but no benchmark exists for AI-painted maps, so transfer to Gemini output is inferred. The PCG route (Create Polygon 2D, Polygon Operation incl. CUT_WITH_PATHS, Shape Grammar, PCG Primitives city examples, 7 Epic PCG skills) is fully present in the local 5.8.1 install and Epic docs, but has never been executed here. On kits: the kit actually measured and placed here is Quixel's free "Medieval Village Megascans Sample" (Fab $0.00, build MedievalGame_5.3, Allows usage with AI: No), not Marco Maria Rossi's paid "Medieval Village"; City Sample, City Sample Buildings and Cassini are $0 Epic samples with explicit 5.8 builds; a handful of free kits allow AI usage (Modular Fantasy Castle CC-BY, UNIBLOCKS) but Fab's JSON exposes no per-build engine version, so 5.8 flags for third-party kits remain unverified. On Gemini: the API free tier has no image generation at all (pricing page, 2026-10-09), so the free path is the Gemini app Basic plan with Nano Banana 2, which adds a visible watermark plus SynthID; Google documents legible text, diagrams and multi-turn iteration, but no official example of a legend-bearing orthographic town map consistent with street views. Corrected: the ground truth's "Fab 403s" (curl with a browser UA gets 200 on the JSON and HTML), the brief's "owned kit now paid", and the playbook's "5.8 build" claims for the Rossi and Sidearm packs.

recommendations: Build the Gemini adapter as a third plan.layout ('image') inside plan_city.py that emits the proven row schema (buildings: loc_cm, size_cm snapped to 50 cm, storeys, yaw_deg, door_side, roof_candidate via roof_servability.py; streets: chained segments <=1500 cm with width_cm) and leaves town_kit_manifest.py, town_kit_place.py, verify, foliage clear, build_street_mask.py and the save/nav/HLOD order untouched; that is the shortest verified critical path.

CV adapter on host Python 3.12 (install shapely 2.2.0, vtracer 0.6.15, sknw 0.15 + numba 0.68.0 into a venv): cv2.kmeans in Lab on the lossless Gemini PNG with a fixed legend palette -> class masks; roads = cv2.ximgproc.thinning(THINNING_GUOHALL) + distanceTransform width + sknw graph, pruned and split into <=15 m segments; footprints = findContours(RETR_CCOMP) + approxPolyDP + shapely minimum_rotated_rectangle snapped to 50 cm; water = mask resampled to city_organic's npz contract (mask bool, origin_cm, cell_m); scale from a prompted scale bar, never from Claude.

Prompt Gemini (app, Basic plan, Nano Banana 2) for a FLAT-COLOUR orthographic plan, not a painting: one fixed palette per class stated as hex values in a legend strip, a labelled 100 m scale bar, north up, no shadows or perspective, then request street-level views in the same multi-turn chat with 'state what must stay identical before what changes'; crop the visible watermark before CV; validate every map against a Watabou PNG+JSON golden set (recall >= 90 %, IoU >= 0.6) before trusting the adapter.

Minimal experiment to prove the PCG route (currently unexecuted): new Blank project, enable PCGPrimitives + PCGToolset; open /PCGPrimitives/Levels/ShapeGrammar_Demo.umap and run City_Generator_Steps_3_Lots; replace its guide splines with three tagged splines from a town_spec; chain Create Polygon 2D -> Polygon Operation (DIFFERENCE / CUT_WITH_PATHS with road ends extended past the district) -> Subdivide_Areas_WithRecursiveSplit -> Assign_ShapeGrammarDefinition with SGD_Bldg_Demo and the L1_* placeholders; count lots and capture an ortho; update 5.8.1 -> 5.8.3 first because of the Polygon Operation attribute-loss fix.

Keep the Quixel Medieval Village Megascans Sample (free, already measured and placed) as the production kit; record its 'Allows usage with AI: No' flag in the licence register and keep R-AIGATE in front of every generator; if an AI-usage-allowed kit is needed, measure Modular Fantasy Castle (CC-BY) or UNIBLOCKS with get_bounds before writing any grammar, and treat their 5.8 compatibility as unverified until the editor loads them.

Read Fab with curl + a Chrome user agent against /i/listings/<uid>, /asset-formats and /i/listings/search (WebFetch 403s); store isAiForbidden, licence names/prices and build names per item in data/licences.json.

Treat Gemini API image generation as unavailable (free tier 'Not available'); plan every image step as an operator action in the Gemini app, recorded as operator-owned AI output in the MANIFEST as already practised, and never feed Fab 'AI: No' meshes to TRELLIS.

refuted: Brief/ground-truth premise 'the Medieval Village pack the user owns (now paid)': the kit measured (Free/_measured/kit_medievalvillage.json, source VaultCache MedievalGame_5.3, modules under /Game/Megascans/3D_Assets) and placed by R-TOWNKIT is Quixel's 'Medieval Village Megascans Sample' (Fab uid 2e11a225, startingPrice 0.0 USD, published 2025-02-03), not Marco Maria Rossi's 'Medieval Village' (uid f89fe420, 29.99/89.99 USD); the owned kit is still free.

Playbook §6.6/§9 'Medieval Village (Marco Maria Rossi) ... 5.7 + 5.8 build' and 'Sidearm Modular Medieval Village: builds for 5.0–5.8' [V]: Fab's asset-formats JSON lists Rossi builds only up to 'Medieval Village 5.7' and Sidearm files 'Medieval Village stylized' / 'Medieval Village stylized 5', with engineVersions null on every file; no 5.8 build is verifiable from the public endpoint.

Ground truth 'Fab HTML pages may 403': only WebFetch gets 403; curl with a Chrome user agent returns HTTP 200 for /i/listings/<uid>, /asset-formats, /i/listings/search and the HTML listing page (which exposes 'Allows usage with AI Yes/No').

Assumption that Gemini free tier includes API image generation: the pricing page (2026-10-09) marks every image model 'Not available' on the Free tier; free generation exists only in the Gemini app (Nano Banana 2, with a visible watermark + SynthID).

Assumption that free Gemini app users get Nano Banana Pro / 2.1 quality (the 'under 10 % text error' figures): the limits page gives Basic 'Image generation with Nano Banana 2' only, 'Redo images with Nano Banana Pro' is Plus/Pro/Ultra, and gemini.google says Nano Banana 2.1 requires a Google AI Plan.

Brief wording 'module catalogue measured in recipes/town_kit.json': town_kit.json holds only roofs, gable and placement constants; the wall/door/corner catalogue is Free/_measured/kit_medievalvillage.json (15 rows) and the module names are hard-coded in scripts/town_kit_plan.py (WALLS/DOORS/CORNER).

Reading Fab's isFree as the price flag: City Sample, Cassini, FANTASTIC Village and the Quixel sample all have startingPrice 0.0 with isFree false, while CC-BY listings have isFree true; use licenses[].priceTier.price / startingPrice.price for 'free'.
Playbook's hint that Fab search results carry the AI flag: the search endpoint's result objects have no isAiForbidden/isAiGenerated keys; the per-listing JSON must be fetched for the flag.
